problem.title: Electron deflected between parallel plates (JEE Main type)
problem.text:
An electron enters the region between two parallel plates (10 V across a 2.0 cm gap)
moving horizontally at 4.0e6 m/s, midway between the plates. The plates are 4.0 cm
long, so the electron spends 1.0e-8 s in the field. How far is it displaced, in total,
by the time it leaves the plates -- and what parabolic path does it trace?
problem.source: Classical charged-particle deflection problem type (JEE Main / HC Verma Concepts of Physics Vol. 2 style); statement rewritten and values chosen for this corpus, not reproduced.

trajectory.integrator: RK4 (exact for constant acceleration; <0.5% phase error on cyclotron orbits at the sampled dt)

timeline.narrate: Place Electron.

because.detail: An electron, with charge and mass fixed by nature rather than by the problem.

timeline.narrate: Place Parallel-plate capacitor.

because.detail: Two oppositely charged plates. Away from the edges the field between them is uniform, which makes this the standard way to produce a known constant field in a problem.

timeline.narrate: Place Environment.

because.detail: The surrounding medium and fields. Defaults are an idealised vacuum with no gravity, which is what textbook electrostatics problems assume -- stated here as an editable value instead of a footnote.

because.law_label: Weight in a uniform gravitational field
because.law_statement: A body of mass m in a uniform gravitational field g experiences a force m*g directed along the field. Uniform is the right idealisation on a bench: g varies by less than a part in a million across a desk.

timeline.narrate: e1: force resolves to [0, 8.011e-17, 0] N.

because.law_statement: The net force on a body is the vector sum of the forces acting on it, each computed as if the others were absent. This is why an electric force and a weight can be derived independently and then added.

timeline.narrate: e1: acceleration resolves to [0, 8.794e13, 0] m/s².

because.law_statement: The net force on a body equals its mass times its acceleration.

timeline.narrate: e1: time is 1.000e-8 s, as stated.
e1: displacement resolves to [0.04, 0.004397, 0] m.

because.law_statement: While acceleration is constant, velocity is linear in time and displacement is quadratic; and v^2 = u^2 + 2*a*s eliminates time entirely.
